thread:
oncall-bot: Pager: Elevated 5xx rate for service inference-gw-private in prod-private-vpc (region: us-west-2). Error spike started ~3549991200. p50 latency 680ms, p95 2.3s, 5xx rate ~9% over last 5m. Dash: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/inf/gw-private?from=now-15m

sara_m: ack — I'm oncall and joining. Pulling logs and routing. Tagging @network-ops and @eng-sre.

raj: seeing a big uptick in SYN retransmits from inference nodes -> upstream transit appliance. Netstat snippet from node-inf-17:```
Active Internet connections (servers and established)
Proto Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address           Foreign Address         State
tcp        0      70 10.10.17.17:443        10.255.1.12:52344        SYN_RECV
```

marta: sFlow and interface counters show drops on transit-appliance-azb-e-0: RxErrors + ifdrops correlated with the spike window.

network-ops: we merged a peering ACL change ~12m ago (PR#4218). Rolling back now as a hypothesis. Notified infra team to pause further peering changes.

eng-sre: can you confirm customer-facing symptoms? @customer-success do we have any customer tickets?

customer-success: we started getting a single enterprise customer (acme-corp) alerting heavy timeouts on private endpoints ~10m ago. They see streaming stalls and reconnects.

sara_m: running a quick traceroute from a failing pod to gateway:```
traceroute to 10.254.0.1 (10.254.0.1), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.17.1  0.3 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
 2  100.64.3.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  transit-appliance-azb  12.1 ms  12.4 ms  12.0 ms
 4  peer-gw  *  *  *
```
peer hop is dropping ICMP — traceroute times out there.

raj: tcpdump on node shows lots of retransmits and some RSTs from peer-gw back to the appliance. Quick tcpdump snippet:```
14:33:12.123456 IP 10.10.17.17.52344 > 10.254.0.1.443: Flags [S], seq 0
14:33:12.223456 IP 10.254.0.1.443 > 10.10.17.17.52344: Flags [R], seq 0
```

marta: interestingly, MTU mismatches can cause stalled streaming but RSTs point to active policy or port exhaustion. I don't see ephemeral port depletion across nodes though.

network-ops: confirming — the peering ACL PR added a deny rule scoped too broadly; it landed before we fully validated the CIDR exceptions. Rolling it back now (revert PR#4218). ETA ~5m.

deploy-bot: Revert PR#4218 applied to peering-acl (deployment id: deploy-8821). No other infra changes detected.

sara_m: after revert, I'm seeing a drop in RSTs but not fully resolved. 5xx rate down from 9% -> 3.4% in last 2m. Still some timeouts.

eng-sre: can we enable temporary fallback routing for private-vpc inference traffic to route through secondary-transit (a different egress path) while we stabilize? That will avoid the peered path.

network-ops: we can add a conditional route for the prefix 10.254.0.0/20 pointing to secondary-transit via route-table rt-priv-shift. Adding now.```
# aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rt-priv-123 --destination-cidr-block 10.254.0.0/20 --gateway-id nat-ss-02
```

raj: applied route change on control-plane; rolling out to affected subnets. Monitoring.

sara_m: immediate effect — p95 latency down to 1.1s, 5xx ~1.2%. Some customers still see intermittent stalls but overall improves. Marking mitigation: traffic routed to secondary-transit.

customer-success: acme-corp reports reduced errors; streaming resumed but they saw 1-2 reconnects during the switch. They're happy with the stabilization for now.

marta: digging into why the revert didn't immediately remove RSTs: transit appliance had some pinned state for the peered sessions. Clearing conntrack on the appliance helped. Running:`sudo conntrack -F` on transit-appliance-azb (coordinated with network-ops).

network-ops: conntrack flush completed on transit-appliance-azb. Observed TCP flows reestablishing cleanly.

raj: after conntrack clear + route shift, 5xx is back to baseline 0.3% over last 3m. No further RSTs observed.

sara_m: switching to monitoring mode. Will keep on this thread for handoff. Preparing quick incident notes for postmortem: suspected root cause — overly broad peering ACL rolled out, caused active RSTs and packet drops; conntrack state prolonged the failure until flushed; fallback route mitigated impact.

tim: recommend adding a pre-merge integration test that simulates peering deny rules against a test prefix and validates ICMP/TCP connectivity (small e2e smoke). Also suggest adding an automated rollback when peering change increases 5xx > 1% within 10m.

eng-sre: agreed on both. Filed follow-ups: INF-987 (add peering smoke test), INF-988 (automated rollback on 5xx spike).

sara_m: handing off to @network-ops for final cleanup and root cause verification. I'll be available for postmortem notes.

network-ops: taking the handoff. We'll validate appliance statefulness, tighten ACL CI, and work with infra to add canary on peering changes.

oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Severity downgraded. Pager silence enabled.

eng-sre: thanks everyone. Postmortem ETA 48h. If anyone has raw captures, drop them into the incident S3 bucket s3://incidents/3549991234/ (sara or network-ops please upload).

customer-success: I've informed acme-corp PM about mitigation and upcoming postmortem. They want a follow-up meeting if the postmortem shows config drift.

sara_m: uploading key logs now. Closing real-time channel here; keeping thread for notes.

marta: one-liner for timeline: peering ACL change -> immediate RSTs/ICMP drop -> customers start timing out -> revert + conntrack flush + route shift -> stable.

eng-sre: applause :thumbsup: Good job on fast rollback + fallback routing. Postmortem will capture lessons and prevention steps.
